title: Clarinet
summary: Limits first: a fixed-pressure model, not a player. Live set (mirror of 2026-11-10): not every live page is the latest render. Some are earlier renders (restored on 2026-11-10, deploys 786 to 788, or never replaced), and each carries only the rows its own page text lists, so counts below that name more pages describe renders that are not live. Of the 23 pages: the reed channel (1.4 mm, separated-jet law) and the removal of the receiver's grid latency are on 10 (A4, Ab3, Bb4, C4, D3, Eb3, Eb5, F3, F5 and Gb5), while the other 13 (A5, Bb3, Bb5, C5, D4, D5, Eb4, F4, G3, G4, G5, Gb3 and Gb4) keep the fully developed viscous slit law and carry no latency removal; the printed contact law is on 21 pages; the printed tone-hole lengths on 16 (A4, Ab3, Bb4, Bb5, C4, C5, D3, D4, D5, Eb4, Eb5, F4, F5, G4, G5 and Gb5); the orifice row on 14 (Ab3, Bb4, C4, C5, D4, Eb4, Eb5, F3, F4, F5, G3, G4, Gb3 and Gb5); the continuation of the hole-length factor above ka = 1 on 7 (A4, Ab3, Bb4, C4, Eb5, F5 and Gb5); the player's tract on 6 (A4, Bb4, D3, Eb3, Eb5 and F3). Bb5 keeps the engine's default contact. A5 (2026-11-03) is the oldest page: a measured reed lay (Pàmies-Vila 2021) in place of the printed contact law, and its page text lists none of the barrel pull, the bore-air profile, the mutual-hole law, the shared outside air or the reed noise. Blown at 1.8 kPa (18.4 cm H2O), under the 20 to 55 cm H2O measured on playing clarinettists (Fuks and Sundberg 1999); at 3.0 to 3.6 kPa a G4 test card has H8 to H12 30 to 32 dB over the recording's (23 at 1.8); nothing is posted there yet. One lumped reed mode on one slit lay; a printed 2-D contact law with a corner at its onset; a reed-noise law that is an extrapolation, so the notes are noisier than the recordings. No lips or vibrato, and no airway except on the pages that carry the player's tract rows (another player's long-tube airway, physics_present[13]). The bore is the published 1981 Buffet Crampon Prestige of Taillard and Sanchez 2016 with its 24 tone holes, the open holes and bell sharing room air (Lefebvre, Scavone and Kergomard 2013), and the bore air follows Noreland's measured temperature profile. One barrel pull of 2.79 mm puts the 19 notes from D3 to G5 at -0.1 c from equal temperament on average, spread 10.0 c, solved without the printed tone-hole lengths; the 19 pages that carry them sounded 0.4 c (G4) to 14.1 c (D3) sharper than they do without them, by harmonic product spectrum on the 15 with-and-without pairs that were measured (Gb4, Bb3, Eb5 and Gb5 have no pair), before the continuation of the hole-length factor above ka = 1 reached these pages, which then moved G4, F4 and Eb4 by 0.40, 0.46 and 0.52 c flat. Fingerings are Moers and Kergomard 2011 Table 2; Gb3 is inferred, Gb5 comes from two printed charts, and F6, from the same charts, speaks a low tone near 324 Hz, so its page stays recording-only. Eighteen pages (Ab3, Bb3, Bb4, C4, C5, D4, D5, Eb4, Eb5, F3, F4, F5, G3, G4, G5, Gb3, Gb4, Gb5) now also carry `open_hole_orifice N` (commit 43ad828c9; commit 453bf176c for G4 and Gb4, whose 14 and 13 open holes are above the old cap of 12 on the coupled holes), the quasi-steady orifice loss on all N of their open holes (N from 2 to 14) in place of the first open hole alone. Each was rendered beside a byte-identical control of its posted card and both were graded on the same library: 13 keep the count, Bb3, D5, G5, Gb5 lose one measure each, Gb4 loses two (pitch and harmonics-to-noise leave the ruler), none gains; the level falls by 0.0 to 5.5 dB, the tone moves by up to 4.4 c, and the render takes 4.3 to 6.4 times the CPU, a fixed cost of the render's build and not of the audio length. The printed tone-hole lengths were then added on top of the orifice row (2026-11-07) on the six of those pages that lacked them: Bb3, Eb5 and Gb4 tie (8, 10 and 9 of 14) and carry them, sounding 5.3, 3.4 and 1.5 c sharper; F3, G3 and Gb3 lose one measure each (8 to 7, 8 to 7 and 9 to 8 of 14, the pitch moving 8.7 to 11.8 c sharp) and stay without them. On A5 (N = 10) and Bb5 (N = 11) the row takes the note away (a low tone near 325 and 339 Hz in place of the note), so those two pages stay as they were, as do A4, Eb3 and D3, which have one open hole or none. The seven pages built before the reed's closure stop (Bb3, Eb3, Eb5, F3, G3, Gb3, Gb4) render the same bytes with the stop in, so the stop changes nothing on them. On 2026-11-08 every page was rendered again with the reed channel corrected (the channel length 1.4 mm that Chatziioannou and van Walstijn 2008 print for their mouthpiece in place of the lay length 0.025 m, and the separated-jet law of van Zon et al. 1990 in place of the fully developed one) and, on the 18 orifice pages, the orifice ports on the coupled network: against the previous versions the loose count falls on 9 pages (Bb5, C5, D4, Eb4, F4, G3, G4, Gb3, Gb4), ties on 12 and rises on 2 (Eb3, Gb5); the level moves by +3.1 to +5.8 dB and the tone by -11.2 to +1.9 c. The posted pages are the corrected ones; every page says what got worse. On 2026-11-08 the receiver's grid latency (a quarter of its grid: 4096 samples, 85.3 ms, on 21 pages; 8192 samples, 170.7 ms, on A4 and Bb4) was removed from the start of every clip on 2026-11-08 with `--compensate-outlet-latency`. On 22 pages the new clip is the previous version's render shifted by those samples, equal to the last bit; on A4 and Bb4 the release tail the old clip cut off is now heard (rms 100.8 and 73.6 LSB over the last 8192 samples); Bb5 is the tip's render, which also moved by the engine between the previous version's build and the build of 2026-11-08 (the flag changes no sample), by -62.3 dB re the clip's rms. The loose count is unchanged on all 23 pages. A player's tract (Kaburagi et al. 2021, participant A, long tube; code 1ace72cd97) was then put upstream of the reed on 23 of them (D3, Eb3, F3, G3, Gb3, Ab3, Bb3, C4, D4, Eb4, F4, Gb4, G4, A4, Bb4, C5, D5, Eb5, F5, Gb5, G5, A5, Bb5): 17 post by the opt-in rule (a tie or a rise). 6 fell and have no page row, tried and left as they were: Ab3 9 to 7 of 14 loose, strict 8 to 6, pitch +0.35 c, largest harmonic change H11 -13.12 dB; C4 9 to 7 of 14 loose, strict 8 to 7, pitch -8.90 c, largest harmonic change H2 +5.19 dB; D4 10 to 9 of 14 loose, strict 9 to 9, pitch -26.05 c, largest harmonic change H8 -16.35 dB; F5 10 to 6 of 15 loose, strict 7 to 5, pitch -1681.40 c, no harmonic comparison, the sounding fundamental left the note's register (702.52 Hz in the control, 265.99 Hz with the tract); Gb5 12 to 5 of 15 loose, strict 10 to 4, pitch -1720.92 c, no harmonic comparison, the sounding fundamental left the note's register (736.37 Hz in the control, 272.51 Hz with the tract); G5 12 to 3 of 15 loose, strict 11 to 2, pitch -1774.29 c, no harmonic comparison, the sounding fundamental left the note's register (780.74 Hz in the control, 280.16 Hz with the tract). See physics_present[13].
physics_present: Air column from the published Buffet Crampon Prestige (1981) bore stations of Taillard and Sanchez 2016, Tableau 2, with all 24 tone holes as side branches at their published positions, minimal diameters and chimney heights, and the mouthpiece as an equivalent cylinder

Fingerings: the open set of each of the 21 normal fingerings from Moers and Kergomard 2011 Table 2, mapped to the Buffet's holes by hole index; Gb3 inferred from the table's rule (F3 with hole 4 also open), a fingering both the Woodwind Fingering Guide's Boehm chart and the UNSW 'Acoustics of the clarinet' diagram now show; Gb5 (written G#5) from those two printed charts
Open tone holes interact across the varying air field (the mutual-hole law, Lefebvre, Scavone and Kergomard 2013), with the open holes and the bell sharing the outside air

Bore air temperature profile measured by Noreland 2013, warm at the barrel and cool at the bell, as a continuous gas field of the exhaled-breath mixture (Coltman 1966, Nederveen 1969); room air outside

Reed: one lumped oscillator with mass, stiffness and damping at the embouchure of Chatziioannou and van Walstijn's Table 1 reed, with the reed channel's separated-jet law (van Zon et al. 1990) at the length 1.4 mm that Chatziioannou and van Walstijn 2008 print for their mouthpiece (not shown to be this Buffet's), on the 10 live pages named in the summary; the other 13 live pages keep the fully developed viscous slit law

Reed contact with the lay: the law printed for this reed (Chatziioannou and van Walstijn, Acta Acustica united with Acustica 98(4), 629-639, 2012: K 6.263e6 N/m^2, exponent 2, onset at 0.16 mm of opening, no contact loss), on 21 live pages; Bb5 keeps the engine's default contact because the printed law scored lower there, and A5 carries a measured lay (Pàmies-Vila 2021)
Reed noise: the duct-constriction law of Oldham and Ukpoho 1990, read at the reed slit with the total pressure drop and the Bernoulli speed
One barrel pull of 2.79 mm, solved once so the 19 notes from D3 to G5 average equal temperament
Blown at one fixed mouth pressure (1800 Pa), rising over 20 ms and released over 60 ms, with a tongue-contact row holding the reed on the lay while the pressure builds
Observer: the physical baffled outlet receiver, open holes and bell summed, room air around the bell and holes, ISO 9613 air absorption

On 16 live pages (A4, Ab3, Bb4, Bb5, C4, C5, D3, D4, D5, Eb4, Eb5, F4, F5, G4, G5 and Gb5), the printed tone-hole lengths (Lefebvre and Scavone 2012): thick-wall inner, matching and radiation lengths and the series inertance of every hole, open or closed. They move every one of those notes sharp, by 0.4 c (G4) to 14.1 c (D3) (harmonic product spectrum, the 15 notes with a with-and-without pair, measured before the continuation above ka = 1); on Eb5 they sit on top of the orifice row (N 5); the live pages of A5, Bb3 and Gb4 are earlier renders without them

Quasi-steady orifice loss at every open hole on 14 live pages (`open_hole_orifice N`, commit 43ad828c9 and 453bf176c, N = the fingering's open holes: Ab3 4, Bb4 2, C4 7, C5 3, D4 9, Eb4 10, Eb5 5, F3 2, F4 12, F5 7, G3 3, G4 14, Gb3 3, Gb5 8): the sharp-edged separation law of the first-hole shunt (c_d 2.69, no threshold velocity), each hole's coefficient reading the gas at that hole, all N solved together through the bore; the ports sit on the coupled network of the interaction row (fs-duct `interaction::port_admittance`, 2026-11-08) and not on independent chimneys; one stated approximation: the sound the holes radiate still comes from the linear network; the sharp-edge premise is not established for this Buffet (its hole edge radii are unmeasured). The other pages keep the first open hole alone (Bb3, D5, G5 and Gb4 carried the row in renders that are no longer live)

The receiver's grid latency (a quarter of its grid: 4096 samples, 85.3 ms, on 21 pages; 8192 samples, 170.7 ms, on A4 and Bb4) was removed from the start of the clips of the 10 live pages that carry the reed channel on 2026-11-08 with `--compensate-outlet-latency`; the other 13 live pages are earlier clips without that removal. On 22 pages the new clip is the previous version's render shifted by those samples, equal to the last bit; on A4 and Bb4 the release tail the old clip cut off is now heard (rms 100.8 and 73.6 LSB over the last 8192 samples); Bb5 is the tip's render, which also moved by the engine between the previous version's build and the build of 2026-11-08 (the flag changes no sample), by -62.3 dB re the clip's rms. The loose count is unchanged on all 23 pages.

The player's tract, upstream of the reed on the clarinet pages named here (card rows `player_tract mouth 0.02`, 40 `player_tract_section` rows, the glottis, `player_tract_wall 15.4 3.79e5 6.22e3` and `player_airway weibel-1963 saab-2021-table-1-B 24`; code 1ace72cd97): participant A's long-tube low-note vocal tract of Kaburagi, Kato, Fukuda and Taguchi 2021 (Acoust. Sci. & Tech. 42(2):83-92), read from the paper's vector plots in 40 equal sections (16.0 cm), then the glottis of the paper's Sec. 4.1, the first 24 generations of Weibel's lung tree (Saab 2021, Table 1, B) and the yielding wall of the voice cards. The card's blowing pressure is one fixed operating point of 1800 Pa, read here as a mouth pressure behind the tract, so the airway's steady resistance leaves it at DC only, through a one-pole of 20 ms, a regulation constant and not a measurement. Each no-row control on the same binary: 23 of 23 are byte-equal to the live raw. physics_missing: No player: no airway or vocal tract of the player (another player's long-tube tract is on the pages named in physics_present[13]), no lips, no vibrato, no wall vibration; the lumped reed has one mode, with no reed continuum and no lip mass or damping

The contact law comes from a 2-D reed model, has a corner at its onset and is not a measured lay profile; its authors write that the fit is 'not accurate for near-closure displacements'. It is not matched to a recording

The reed-noise law was measured on dampers and orifice plates in a 300 mm duct at 10 to 25 m/s and does not fix the jet speed or pressure drop to use for a slit this small; that choice alone moves the source by up to 40 dB. The notes are noisier than the recordings (harmonics-to-noise 21.3 to 44.4 dB against 30.6 to 47.0 dB on the 23 live pages with both values) and the level is not a prediction

The barrel pull sets the mean, not the spread: the 10.0 c spread about equal temperament is mostly this specimen's own playing pattern (Taillard and Sanchez 2016, Fig. 7, read from the figure, spreads 7 c over D3 to G5). The aim was equal temperament, not the recordings, and the pull is one step for every note

Pad height, undercuts, key geometry and the tone-hole edge radius are unmeasured for this Buffet, as are the mouthpiece interior (chamber, baffle, throat, lay) and the reed and mouthpiece the recordings used

The printed tone-hole length corrections (Lefebvre and Scavone 2012) on Eb3, F3, G3 and Gb3: on each of those four they lower the grader count by one (Eb3 alone; F3, G3 and Gb3 also with the orifice row on, 8 to 7, 8 to 7 and 9 to 8 of 14), so those pages are rendered without them. Bb3, Eb5 and Gb4, which lost one when the row was tried alone, tie with the orifice row under it and carry it. On the 19 pages that carry them the count ties on 17 and rises on two, Bb5 (8 to 9 of 14) and Gb5 (11 to 12 of 15)
The recordings (University of Iowa Musical Instrument Samples) are another clarinet and player: there is no same-specimen comparison

Only the 21 normal fingerings of Moers and Kergomard 2011 Table 2 are printed there. Gb3 is inferred, not printed; Gb5 and F6 take their hole states from two other printed charts (UNSW; Woodwind Fingering Guide) by a mapping of drawn holes to the Buffet's that is a judgment, checked on 17 of the 17 decodable printed fingerings, and UNSW draws 'a Bb clarinet', not this Buffet. The card has no altissimo leak physics

F6 does not speak: with its printed fingering the card sounds a low tone near 324 Hz with a weak line at F6's own frequency 30 dB under it; the cause has not been isolated. The orifice row on every open hole brings a low tone of the same kind on A5 (N = 10: a 325 Hz line 8 dB over the note, 8 of 15 inside the ruler falling to 4) and Bb5 (N = 11: only a 339 Hz line, 9 of 14 falling to 3); a plane-wave transfer-matrix estimate of the cards' bores (a check of the author's, not the engine's operator) puts the first impedance peak at 340 Hz on A5, 355 Hz on Bb5 and 341 Hz on F6, 4.4 to 5.0 % above the three tones; in 0.9 s trials A5 loses the note from three coupled holes (the vent and the next two) and Bb5 from two (the vent and the next), and the level is flat beyond that; the coupled port network (2026-11-08) does not return the note (A5 with three ports: the strongest line is 325 Hz and the note is 7.2 dB under it, 7.1 dB on the independent network; Bb5 with two: 339 Hz, 15.0 dB under, 14.9), and with the interaction row off the note stays (875 and 920 Hz), so the loss belongs to the coupled base with the ports on and not to the independent-port formulation; why the row hands the oscillation to the low tone is not shown

Every clarinet card ends in a flanged (infinite-baffle) radiation load, because the receiver used needs one; a real bell is unbaffled. At D3 the low-ka unflanged law raises the bore's impedance peaks by about 3 dB (2.8 dB, mean of the peaks between 0.6 and 1.9 kHz, re the playing peak); that law refuses above ka 1, about 1.9 kHz
The sharp-edge premise of the orifice row is not measured for this Buffet's holes (their edge radii are unmeasured), so the row is a consistency fix and not a calibration

The reed channel: 1.4 mm is the length printed for the mouthpiece of Chatziioannou and van Walstijn 2008, not shown to be this Buffet's, and the separated-jet law of van Zon et al. 1990 is the print's own two-dimensional, quasisteady, laminar one (measured on a 3 cm square pipe with h = 1 mm and L = 4 or 8 mm; the S = 2h fit is within 3 % of its data for Re up to 4000). Its eq. 7 is inconsistent with its eq. 5, so the Poiseuille part is a construction from its eqs. 1, 5 and 6 that matches its Fig. 2 theory curve to 0.011 at fifteen read points. The law switches at L/h = 3 (an opening of 0.467 mm) in a step for which the print gives no blend; the reed opening did not reach it on any page. Unsteady channel inertia is not modelled.

The player's own tract on these pages: the tract is another player's (a professional saxophonist, participant A), measured with the player's mouthpiece on a uniform vinyl tube (28 cm for the long tube) and not on a saxophone body, under a clarinet card; its MRI pitch (201 Hz) differs from the pitch of the pages (+547 c on D3 to -2626 c on Bb5, positive where 201 Hz lies above the page's pitch); the posture for each note is not stated in the text as read; the card's 1800 Pa is a model's fixed operating point, under the 20 to 55 cm H2O measured on playing clarinettists, read here as a mouth pressure behind the tract; the 20 ms one-pole that takes the airway's steady resistance out of it is a regulation constant, not a measurement; no tract was measured on the recorded player, and no mechanism is claimed for the pitch and harmonic changes.
blocked: F6 (written G6): the card speaks a low tone near 324 Hz instead of F6, so its page stays recording-only until the cause is found
